Pilot privacy

Last updated 18 October 2026

Pilot runs on your Mac. It has no account, no analytics and no crash-reporting service, and it never sends anything to its maker. It goes online only for the features in the table below, and only when you use them.

What stays on your Mac

  • Your clipboard history, the file index, your binds and settings, notes and snippets.
  • Dictation and Read aloud: your voice and the text run on the Mac. Only the models are downloaded, once.
  • Text found in images (Apple's Vision) and image upscaling.
  • AI keys you add, which live in the macOS Keychain.
  • Pilot's own log, which stays in macOS's log on your Mac.

When Pilot goes online

WhereWhenWhat is sent
api.anthropic.com, api.openai.com, openrouter.ai, or an address you typeQuick AI, the AI chat and AI on selected text, only after you add a key or pick a providerYour question, the text you selected and any screenshot you attach, with your own key
Your own Claude Code or Codex appWhen you pick it as the AIWhatever that app sends, under your own plan
api.giphy.com and GIPHY's image serversGIF search, after you add a GIPHY keyYour search words; the GIFs come back
cdn.jsdelivr.net, then latest.currency-api.pages.devCurrency conversion in the calculator, at most every 12 hoursA request for today's rates; nothing about you
api.ipify.orgStats › public address, if you turn it on; every 10 minutes while shownA plain request; the answer is your public address
api.github.com, itunes.apple.com, registry.npmjs.org, crates.io, pypi.org, proxy.golang.orgWhen you search in InstallYour search words
The pictures beside Install's resultsWhen a result shows oneA request for that picture: App Store artwork, a GitHub avatar or the app's site icon
The address of what you installWhen you install something from InstallThe download, or the tool doing the install (Homebrew, npm and the like) contacting its own servers. Pilot shows the command first
raw.githubusercontent.comWhen you browse the extension catalogue, or install Homebrew from InstallFile requests
huggingface.coThe first time you use dictation, a Read aloud voice or the larger upscalerModel downloads; nothing about you
The site you make a web app fromInstall › Web AppRequests for that site's page and icon
Apple's speed-test serversWhen you run Test internet speed (macOS's own networkQuality)Test traffic
Pilot's update feedOnce a day, only after you say yes to update checksPilot's version and your macOS version, as Sparkle sends them

Search the web, quick links and web apps open the site in your browser or in the web app, which then talks to that site as any browser would.

An extension is a program you choose to install. Pilot shows the addresses it says it connects to before you install it. Install only extensions you trust.

Open source

Pilot is open source under the MIT licence, so anyone can check this page against the code: github.com/banozz0/pilot.

Report a privacy issue

Open an issue at github.com/banozz0/pilot/issues. If Pilot ever contacts an address this page does not list, that is a bug: please report it.
